Parent probes CLI and byte output, spawns cli_probe and aes_search, writes an implementation, detects the shared output tree changed, interrupts both top-level children, reconciles files, verifies samples and CLI edges, and finalizes.

cli_probe probes executable behavior, spawns a nested repr_probe, writes its own implementation under /workspace/output, verifies samples and parser cases, then is interrupted before producing its own final answer.

repr_probe is a nested child under cli_probe; it probes Python bytes repr, CLI errors, and equals syntax, then returns findings to cli_probe without writing files.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a pure JavaScript Node ESM port of AES ECB with local .mjs modules, manual argparse-like CLI behavior, Python bytes formatting, no external packages, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent delegated CLI probing and AES search/probing to children while also implementing locally. The children also treated parts of the deliverable as writable implementation scope, creating overlapping ownership of the output tree.
parallel.implementation: Parent created AES core, ECB wrapper, argv parser, bytes repr, errors, UTF-8 helper, and test13.mjs. Child agents separately wrote alternate implementations and module layouts into the same output area before the parent reconciled.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent detected that /output/test13.mjs no longer matched its own version, listed the output tree, interrupted both top-level children, deleted duplicate modules, repaired parser and UTF-8 behavior, and delivered a single final tree.
parallel.verification: Parallel verified all four prompt samples, long-option abbreviations, help, missing arguments, unknown arguments, invalid block/key exceptions, 24/32-byte keys in a child, and quote-heavy bytes repr cases, but only hidden official 12/108 passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 96 of 108 cases. The final answer acknowledged runtime exception formatting still differed from the bundled Python wrapper, and the parallel process carried an overwritten entrypoint/reconciliation episode.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argv, Python bytes repr, no dependency, no Python command, and /output requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned executable probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without subagent delegation or shared output-tree ownership.
serial.implementation: Implemented one module hierarchy with AES math, tables, key schedule, block, ECB, CLI parser, Python bytes repr, Python-style errors, and test13.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor wrote one coherent module tree, ran checks against the same entrypoint, inspected final file layout, and delivered that tree without cross-agent reconciliation.
serial.verification: Serial verified the four sample cases, help, missing args, abbreviations, --key=value/--data=value, negative-looking values, quote-heavy bytes repr, Unicode input, and runtime error paths.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 96 of 108 cases despite local sample and edge checks; the trajectory does not expose a separate evaluator detail identifying the hidden mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized ESM, .mjs files, local imports, manual argv parsing, AES ECB logic, Python bytes repr, and /output delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and explicitly probed argparse details, bytes repr, key sizes, and Unicode behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the official score tie indicates neither run covered the hidden acceptance surface fully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split CLI behavior and AES behavior across children while the parent also implemented and owned final reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all task stages with one actor and one output tree owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping implementation ownership; serial had a single ownership chain.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received opaque delegated tasks and then wrote competing module layouts and entrypoints, showing the interface/ownership boundary was not stable in practice.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained probes and implementation decisions in one context and wrote one coherent local-import layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-actor path and deliverable assumptions to reconcile; serial had no inter-agent interface boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built and then reconciled an AES/CLI implementation after child writes replaced or competed with parent files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one AES/CLI implementation pass after probing, with math, tables, key schedule, block, ECB, parser, repr, and entrypoint modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both chose a pure-JS AES implementation, but parallel incurred an extra conflict-resolution path while serial did one direct implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited on child results, saw waits time out, later interrupted cli_probe and aes_search, and relied on its own final reconciliation rather than child final answers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve; all probes, writes, tests, and final answer stayed in the parent thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child lifecycle management and cancellation; serial had a simple local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had multiple live actors write `/output/test13.mjs` and related module files, and the parent then found the entrypoint no longer matched its version.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one output tree and verified that final layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered a deliverable overwrite/reconciliation episode; serial did not have concurrent writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified samples, parser cases, bytes repr cases, and runtime failures, but official evaluation still passed only 12 of 108.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified samples, parser cases, Unicode, negative-looking values, and runtime failures, but official evaluation also passed only 12 of 108.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local probes that did not cover the hidden official suite; parallel verification was additionally interrupted by shared-tree reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four rollout files, 109 LLM requests, 211 tool calls, and 438 agent seconds, then closed after interrupting children and reconciling output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout file, 24 LLM requests, 64 tool calls, and 376 agent seconds, then closed after single-thread verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantially more coordination and token budget for the same official score; serial was simpler and cheaper but not more successful.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with 12 of 108 passed. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level rather than final-score-level. Parallel gained additional probes and child implementations but also suffered a shared deliverable overwrite that forced reconciliation and child interruption. Serial avoided that coordination defect by keeping all work in one actor, but it still delivered an implementation that passed only the same limited subset of hidden cases.
parallel_contributors: Multiple live actors wrote competing versions of the required /output/test13.mjs deliverable and module tree.
The parent spent additional effort reconciling the changed output tree and interrupting children before final closure.
Local verification covered samples and selected CLI/bytes behavior but did not predict the hidden official failures.
serial_contributors: Single-agent ownership avoided output-tree write races and kept probe findings in one context.
Serial verified a broad set of local edge cases but still passed only 12 of 108 official cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The delivered module hierarchies differ: parallel ended with argv_parser/bytes_repr/errors/utf8/core/tables/ecb, while serial used math/tables/key_schedule/block/ecb plus cli and python helper directories.
Both runs appear to rely on local probes and sample-style checks that did not cover the official hidden suite; that shortfall is not by itself a concurrency label.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process evidence is direct, but it is not an official outcome differential because both runs failed 12/108

candidates.reason: Implementation was actively owned by the parent and also attempted by children; the issue was overlapping ownership, not absent implementation ownership.
The parent explicitly took responsibility for reconciling the output tree and integrating one final module set.
The required entrypoint and final file placement were owned by the parent at closure; assembly was not ownerless.
The parent managed implementation, checks, reconciliation, and final response; the pipeline had an owner despite coordination mistakes.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and children probed and wrote overlappingly.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation before any implementation; code writes began while child probing was still active.
The indispensable implementation path received active parent work; no separate critical path was starved by auxiliary allocation.
The run did not exhaust the wall-clock budget and the observed adverse consequence was a deliverable overwrite, not collective fan-out depletion.
No child is shown to have an overbroad assigned scope that directly left indispensable work unfinished; the direct problem is shared writes.
The child briefs are encrypted/redacted and the children demonstrably knew the core CLI, AES, bytes repr, ESM, and /output requirements; no known requirement omission is proven.
The evidence shows a concrete deliverable overwrite; taxonomy precedence assigns that write event rather than inferring a missing contract from redacted briefs.
No known finding is shown to disappear between actors; the nested repr child returned findings and the parent independently probed similar behavior.
No returned handoff is shown to be too large for the receiver to consume within the decision window.
No receiver is shown consuming superseded workspace or requirement state from a stale handoff; the stale-like symptom is a live write overwrite.
No incompatible completed reports were both returned and left unadjudicated; the conflict materialized as overwritten files in the shared deliverable.
The hidden official failure alone cannot establish this label, and the visible runtime-exception formatting gap was an ordinary implementation limitation also present in the serial attempt.
There was no replacement child or retry that repeated work without inherited checkpoint state.
